candidates.title: "ValueError: Value out of range" when uploading large files (~>= 4.5GB) with `st.file_uploader`
candidates.text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a `.streamlit/config.toml` file to set the upload limit to 4.5 GB:

    ```toml
    [server]
    maxUploadSize = 4500
    ```
2. Create a 4.4 GB file:
    ```sh
    truncate -s 4280m example.file
    ```
3. Run the above app and upload `example.file` to the file uploader widget

candidates.title: file_uploader API docstrings 1.49.0
candidates.text:
## file_uploader (line 252)

Display a file uploader widget.
By default, uploaded files are limited to 200 MB each. You can
configure this using the ``server.maxUploadSize`` config option. For
more information on how to set config options, see |config.toml|_.

.. |config.toml| replace:: ``config.toml``
.. _config.toml: https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/configuration/config.toml

Parameters
----------
label : str
    A short label explaining to the user what this file uploader is for.
    The label can optionally contain GitHub-flavored Markdown of the
    following types: Bold, Italics, Strikethroughs, Inline Code, Links,
    and Images. Images display like icons, with a max height equal to
    the font height.

    Unsupported Markdown elements are unwrapped so only their children
    (text contents) render. Display unsupported elements as literal
    characters by backslash-escaping them. E.g.,
    ``"1\. Not an ordered list"``.

    See the ``body`` parameter of |st.markdown|_ for additional,
    supported Markdown directives.

    For accessibility reasons, you should never set an empty label, but
    you can hide it with ``label_visibility`` if needed. In the future,
    we may disallow empty labels by raising an exception.

candidates.title: file_uploader limit number of uploaded files
candidates.section: file_uploader limit number of uploaded files
candidates.text:
file_uploader limit number of uploaded files

with `st.file_uploader(accept_multiple_files=True)`
I can limit the **size** of files but not **number of files**.

### Problem
Some people spam upload which crashes app. (Because the file upload size limit is per file)

### Solution
st.file_uploader(accept_multiple_files=True, max_number_files=50)

### Additional context
Would be nice to also support a hard limit in config.
```toml
# Max size, in megabytes, for files uploaded with the file_uploader.
# Default: 200
maxUploadSize = 200
maxNumberFiles = 100
```

---
